terra.problem: The line about grabbing familiar-looking things in the dark has no clear connection to the answer, so the joke does not make sense.
The dough-bowl comparison does not match the action: looking for a chocolate chip is not like adding an unsupported reason to Scripture.
The cookie comparison does not work. Half a recipe can make a smaller batch; it does not necessarily make a flat cookie.
Moses does not say the same thing twice. He gives two distinct prohibitions: eating the meat and touching the carcass.
Calling clean the 'wrong direction' says the baker's answer is wrong, which Papa Dorin must not do.
The joke says every baker knows a tenth when they see one, which can make a baker who missed the answer feel put down.
The passage says every three years; it does not say that a third appears as a time.
Calling the baker's selection 'a funny thing to guess' makes the answer, rather than Papa Dorin himself, the target of the joke.
The line places Moses in the middle of a feast, but he is giving instructions about a feast, not described as being at one.
'Within your gates' places the Levite within their towns, not necessarily at the gates.
'A good last line for this stop' refers to the lesson's structure, which Papa Dorin must not discuss.
